chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who performs salat (prayer) and does not take his hands out of his garment, so he said:
"If he takes his hands out, then it is good; and if he does not take his hands out, then there is no harm."

key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) without taking the hands out of one's garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning prayer attire and posture during salat (prayer). It indicates that taking the hands out of one's garment in prayer is preferable, but leaving them inside does not invalidate the prayer and carries no problem.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.826 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man praying without taking his hands out of his garment.
The Imam said: "If he takes his hands out, it is good, but if he does not, there is no issue (no problem)."
